cards.front: State whether shoe size is discrete or continuous.
back: Discrete: the recorded values occur in separate allowed steps, not any real value in an interval.

cards.front: Find the mode of 3, 5, 5, 7, 8, 8, 8, 10.
For 4, 7, 7, 10, 12, find the mean and median.
back: The ordered middle value is 7, so the median is 7.

cards.front: A survey of 120 people has 35 choosing cycling. Find the angle for cycling in a pie chart.
back: The fraction is 35/120.

cards.front: A school has 600 students, including 150 in Year 11. A proportional stratified sample contains 80 students. How many should be from Year 11?
back: Year 11 forms 150/600 = 1/4 of the population.
Select 80 × 1/4 = 20 Year 11 students randomly within that stratum.

cards.front: A student estimates the whole school’s favourite sport by questioning only the football team. Explain the problem and suggest an improvement.
back: The team is not representative of the school; football is likely to be overrepresented.
Use a random sample from the whole school or appropriate randomly sampled strata.

cards.front: A data set has lower quartile 18, median 24 and upper quartile 31. Find its interquartile range and interpret it.
back: The middle 50% of the data span 13 units.

cards.front: A line of best fit uses data for ages 10 to 16. Explain why predicting a value at age 14 is generally safer than at age 30.
back: Age 14 is within the observed range, so the estimate is interpolation.
Age 30 is extrapolation far beyond the data; the relationship may not continue.

cards.front: A histogram class 10 < x ≤ 15 has frequency 18. Another class 15 < x ≤ 25 has frequency 24. Find their frequency densities and explain which bar is taller.
back: First class width = 5, so density = 18/5 = 3.6.
Second class width = 10, so density = 24/10 = 2.4.
The first bar is taller even though it contains fewer values. In a histogram, area represents frequency.

cards.front: Eight parcels have mean mass 2.5 kg. Three of them have mean mass 1.5 kg. Find the mean mass of the other five parcels.
back: Mass of all eight = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg.
Mass of the three = 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 kg.
The other five total 15.5 kg, so their mean is 15.5/5 = 3.1 kg.

cards.front: Salaries in a small business are £20000, £22000, £23000, £25000 and £150000. Find the mean and median. Explain which better describes a typical salary here.
back: The median is £23000.
The very high salary pulls up the mean, so the median better describes the typical employee in this set.

cards.front: A bar chart compares values 90 and 100, but its vertical axis starts at 80. Explain why it may exaggerate the difference and how to improve it.
back: The visible bar heights are proportional to 10 and 20, making one appear twice the other.
The actual values are 90 and 100, so the second is only about 11.1% greater.
Use a zero baseline for bars, or display the values and any axis break clearly without implying bar-length proportionality.

cards.front: How do you choose a median from an ordered list with an even number of values?
back: Average the two middle values.

cards.front: What is frequency density?
back: Frequency divided by class width. Histogram bar area, rather than height alone, represents frequency.

cards.front: Why plot cumulative frequency at upper class boundaries?
back: Each plotted total counts values up to that boundary. Start at the first lower boundary with cumulative frequency zero.

cards.front: What does a box plot show?
back: The minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum, using the convention in the question.

cards.front: How should two distributions be compared?
back: Compare a suitable measure of centre and a measure of spread, using numerical evidence in context.

cards.front: What is the difference between a bar chart and a histogram?
back: Bar charts show categories or discrete values, usually with gaps. Histograms use adjacent intervals for grouped numerical data, with frequency represented by area.

cards.front: How should a line of best fit be drawn?
back: Follow the overall trend with points roughly balanced around it. Do not join every point or force it through the origin.

cards.front: Why use midpoints when estimating a grouped mean?
back: Individual values are unknown, so a representative value is needed for each interval; this makes the resulting mean an estimate.

cards.front: How can an outlier affect the mean and median?
back: An extreme value can strongly change the mean. The median depends on position and is usually less affected.

cards.front: What distinguishes a census from a sample?
back: A census attempts to collect data from the whole population. A sample uses only part of it.

cards.front: What makes a random sample different from choosing whoever is convenient?
back: A defined random selection procedure gives members the intended chance of selection; convenience can systematically exclude groups.

cards.front: When is a pictogram key essential?
back: When each symbol represents a specified number of items. Interpret partial symbols using that key.
